title: Kevin Hern Stock Trades: 71+ Transactions in One Disclosure (Sep 2026)
content:
Rep. Kevin Hern (OK-01) disclosed at least 71 distinct trades in a single filing on September 25, 2026: 67 sales, 2 purchases and 2 exchanges, covering transactions from August 27 to September 15.

Trade data: Bargo, compiled from U.S. House and Senate STOCK Act filings.

Ranges are the sum of the low and high bounds across distinct lines for each ticker. Price change is Bargo's comparison of the sale-date price with the October 2 price. *Bargo lists a third, identical Rockwell row; counting it would make the range $45K–$150K.

What's been disclosed

  • One filing: All trades were disclosed on September 25. Transactions are dated August 27 through September 15.
  • Row count: Bargo's data lists 77 rows for this filing. Six of them exactly repeat another row, which leaves 71 distinct trades: 67 sales, 2 purchases and 2 exchanges.
  • Largest positions by reported range in this table: Devon Energy ($330K–$850K across 5 sale lines), then Illinois Tool Works ($95K–$250K across 4 sale lines).

Quick FAQ

Why does the post say 71 when the data has 77 rows?
Six rows are exact copies of another row. The data does not show whether they are duplicate entries or separate transactions with identical details, so we count 71 as the minimum number of distinct trades.

Why are so many trades disclosed on one day?
A periodic transaction report can cover several weeks of trades at once, as long as each trade is reported within the 45-day window set by the STOCK Act.

Does the filing say why the trades were made?
No. Filings list the asset, the type of transaction, the date and a value range, not a reason.

Why are the amounts in the table ranges?
Filings report value bands rather than exact amounts, so the table adds up the low and high bounds of each line.
